### `cloud eval list`

List the eval suites saved in a project.

| Fl
ag | Required | Description |\n| - | - | - |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently

updated project) |

### `cloud eval run`

Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run it.
Provide **either** `--suite` **or** `--file`, not both.\n\nBy default the command prints a launch receipt and returns immediately
. `--wait` polls every launched run to a terminal state.\n\n**Exit codes (`--wait` only).** Without `--wait` this command's exit c
ode is unchanged: `0` on any launch, `1` on a partial or wholly failed fan-out. `--wait` owns a separate six-code contract — a cal

ler who asked this process to sit and watch a run to completion is asking it to say how the run went:

| Code | Meaning |
| - |
- |\n| `0` | Every waited run passed, unanimously, and (when a report was requested) every report was assembled |\n| `1` | A run
**completed** with a **failed** verdict. The only condition that produces this code |\n| `2` | Usage error — bad flags, `--reporte
r`/`--out` without `--wait`, or an invalid suite file (after auth, before any server/model work) |\n| `3` | Auth failed — no crede
ntial, or the platform rejected it, at launch or mid-wait (a token that expired during a long poll). Zero credits spent if it happ
ened before launch |\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed before evaluation — a launch failure this CLI itself observed (network, time
out, rate limit, a partial or failed fan-out, an unrecognized launch error), or a local `--out` write failure — unless a more seve
re outcome (`1` or `3`) already applies to the same run, per the merge order above |\n| `5` | No valid verdict — `inconclusive`, a
null/unrecognized result, a run whose own status is failed/cancelled/timed-out, a wait that hit its deadline, a mid-wait failure
that was not auth-shaped, or a report that could not be assembled |\n\nNo infrastructure condition ever maps to `1` — see the same
rule under `eval gate` below. A multi-target launch merges these worst-of across every waited run, in the order `1 > 3 > 4 > 5 >
0`: a real verdict failure is never masked by a sibling's infrastructure noise, and a credential failure (which may be *why* other
targets show no verdict) outranks a plain connection failure.\n\nThis six-code contract is new and deliberately **different** fro
m `eval gate`'s four codes below — see that command's own doc for why the two are not unified. An invalid suite file exits **2** e
ither way — `eval validate` still exits 1 for the same contract failure, because it is a verdict on the file and this command is n

ot.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes, unless `--file` | Eval suite name or ID |
\n| `--file <path>` | Yes, unless `--suite` | Versioned suite file to upload and run (`.yaml` or `.json`, or `-` for stdin) |\n| `
--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--server <id-or-name...>`
| No | Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only) |\n| `--environment <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached projec
t environment(s) to run. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached client(s) to
run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--host <id-or-name...>` |
No | **Deprecated** alias for `--client`. Passing both is an error. Not the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam compat --host` / `mcpja
m tools --host` take — see [Two different `--host` flags](#two-different---host-flags). |\n| `--all-targets` | No | Run **every**
attached environment (or, if none, every attached host) — one **paid run per target** |\n| `--iterations <n>` | No | Run each case
this many times (1-10), for this run only |\n| `--repetitions <n>` | No | **Legacy** spelling of `--iterations`. Passing both is
an error. |\n| `--case <id-or-title...>` | No | Run only these cases instead of the whole suite |\n| `--exclude-skills` | No | Run
the \"without skills\" A/B arm: nothing is pinned, and the run is labelled as excluded |\n| `--refresh-snapshot` | No | **Persist
s a new host-config snapshot on the suite** (see below). Single-target runs only. |\n| `--notes <text>` | No | Free-text note stor
ed on the run |\n| `--min-pass-rate <n>` | No | Pass threshold for this run (0-100), overriding the suite's own |\n| `--match-opti
ons <json>` | No | Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. `'{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'` |\n| `--idempotency-key <key>` | N
o | Retry key for a lost launch response. For `--file`, a fresh key is minted and printed on every invocation when this flag is om
itted; supply the printed key to replay the same run instead of starting a new one |\n| `--wait` | No | Wait for every launched ru
n to reach a terminal status |\n| `--wait-timeout <ms>` | No | Maximum wait time (default 2100000); requires `--wait` |\n| `--repo
rter <json-summary\\|junit-xml\\|html>` | No | Write the completed structured report to stdout; requires `--wait`. `html` is a sel
f-contained decision summary + failures page — traces/parity/history are not included. |\n| `--out <path>` | No | Atomically write
the completed report to a file; defaults to `json-summary`, or uses `--reporter` when present; requires `--wait` |\n| `--compose-
client <id-or-name>` | No | Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved environment (see below). **Ephemeral by default** — p
ass `--save-targets` to attach it to the suite. |\n| `--compose-host <id-or-name>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--compose-clie
nt` |\n| `--compose-computer <id-or-name>` | No | Sandbox image to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-model <id...>` | No |
Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces the client's pinned model unless `--with-client-default` is set |\n| `--compose-m
odel-selection <json...>` | No | Whole saved model selection(s) — source, connection, `settings.reasoningEffort` — as JSON: one ce
ll per selection, for its model, at its effort. Repeat to add several selections for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each di
stinct selection is its own cell |\n| `--with-client-default` | No | Also launch an inherit cell using each client's pinned model,
alongside `--compose-model` |\n| `--compose-server <id-or-name...>` | No | Server(s) to pin on the composed stack, snapshotted in
to a server group so a rerun keeps testing them. Mutually exclusive with `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-server-group <id
>` | No | Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-host-servers` | No | **No longer supported** — reje
cted. An eval run takes its servers from a server group alone; use `--compose-server` or `--compose-server-group` |\n| `--compose-
skill <id...>` | No | Project-shared skill IDs to pin on the composed stack |\n| `--compose-secret <id...>` | No | Project secret
IDs the composed stack grants to its runs (`secrets list` shows them) |\n| `--save-targets` | No | Attach the composed environment

s to the suite (append, capped at 10). Without it the stack is ephemeral |

#### Composing a target instead of naming one

`--
compose-client <id-or-name>` builds an execution stack for this run instead of\nnaming a saved environment, refined by `--compose-
computer`, `--compose-model`,\n`--compose-server-group`, `--compose-skill` and `--compose-secret`. The stack becomes an unnamed,\n
content-addressed environment (the same one `environments ensure-adhoc`\nproduces), so composing the same stack twice reuses one e

nvironment.
`--compose-host` is the deprecated spelling of the same flag.

`--compose-model` and `--compose-secret` carry the d
eployment requirement\ndescribed under [Deployment support for model overrides and secret\ngrants](#deployment-support-for-model-o
